trust_decision.summary: Whether an outbound plain-DNS message may carry a caller-supplied zero transaction ID over UDP: decided in upstream/plain.go dialExchange, where a zero ID must be replaced by a random one for UDP only and the caller's original ID restored on the response.

landing_point.why: The summary names a DoQ-to-UDP path, so an engineer looks first at the DoQ server handler that unpacks the client message and hands it to the resolver; the ID-0 requirement is documented right there (proxy/serverquic.go:339-345).

fix_sites.entry_point: upstream.(*plainDNS).Exchange, the exported Upstream API (upstream/plain.go:139), reached from the DoQ listener (proxy/serverquic.go:253-287), the DoH listener (proxy/serverhttps.go:177-184), the plain UDP listener (proxy/serverudp.go:147-159), the plain TCP listener (proxy/servertcp.go:179-187) and Proxy.LookupNetIP (proxy/lookup.go:32-36)
new helper setRequestForNetwork, called only from upstream/plain.go dialExchange

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RFC 9250 and RFC 8484 make ID 0 the expected shape for DoQ/DoH (proxy/serverquic.go:339-345 deliberately accepts any ID; upstream/doh.go:154-167 and upstream/doq.go:171-184 zero it by design), so a solver can call a zero ID legitimate and leave the DoQ-to-UDP path as it is.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The response returned to the caller must keep the caller's original message ID: the DoQ/DoH servers write d.Res back to the client, and a caller-supplied nonzero ID must not be replaced (upstream/dot.go:211-213 and upstream/plain_internal_test.go:41-67 both treat a response ID differing from the request ID as an error). A fix that mutates req.Id in place instead of copying and restoring breaks that contract and races with concurrent users of the same message.

O6_input_shapes: dns.Msg with Id == 0 (DoQ clients per RFC 9250, DoH clients per RFC 8484, and Proxy.LookupNetIP requests built with SetQuestion)
dns.Msg with a non-zero caller ID (must be forwarded unchanged and must not be rewritten in place)
network UDP vs network TCP: only UDP gets the new ID, TCP keeps the original
truncated UDP answer, which retries over TCP with the unmodified request

O7_producer.where: proxy/serverquic.go:253-282 (DoQ handler unpacks a client message whose ID is normally 0) and proxy/lookup.go:32 (SetQuestion leaves Id 0)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second plain-DNS message-writing implementation next to the TLS one, which would need its own zero-ID handling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dot.go already builds and checks DNS messages by hand (dns.Conn.WriteMsg/ReadMsg plus an explicit reply.Id != req.Id check), so a maintainer splitting plain.go into a pooled or connected exchange would naturally copy that shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: normalising the DoQ request (for example re-randomising d.Req.Id) in the server handler before it reaches the resolver
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: AdGuard Home historically zeroed IDs at the DoQ server, and this handler already owns the DoQ-specific protocol rules, so a maintainer could put the fix here as a composition wrapper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a direct lookup path that constructs its own message (Id 0 from SetQuestion) and exchanges it outside Proxy.Resolve
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This helper already fabricates DNS messages in the proxy layer rather than the upstream layer; adding a fast path for internal A/AAAA or PTR lookups is a small, plausible change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a bootstrap resolver that sends its own plain UDP queries to bootstrap addresses instead of going through upstream.plainDNS
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The bootstrap package owns dialing and hostname resolution and is deliberately independent of package upstream, so a resolver added there would duplicate message construction and could keep ID 0.

O9_family: insufficient randomness in the outbound DNS transaction ID (off-path spoofing / cache-poisoning class), CWE-330, with CWE-362/CWE-662 concerns around mutating a caller-shared message

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.26.1 at the pinned commit (go.mod:3), Makefile GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.1; module github.com/AdguardTeam/dnsproxy with deps fetched from proxy.golang.org
O10_build.project_tests: upstream/plain_internal_test.go:18-67 and :69+ run against a local UDP/TCP test DNS server (startDNSServer), including TestUpstream_plainDNS, TestUpstream_plainDNS_badID and TestUpstream_plainDNS_fallbackToTCP; proxy/proxy_internal_test.go:593 TestExchangeWithReservedDomains covers routing; upstream/upstream_internal_test.go:119-234 TestUpstreams performs real exchanges with public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, tls://..., quic://...), so the full suite is not offline even though the affected plain-UDP behaviour is exercisable on loopback.

j.j_sites_touched: internal/cmd/proxy.go, proxy/errors.go, proxy/errors_plan9.go, upstream/doh.go, upstream/doq.go, upstream/plain.go, upstream/upstream.go
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Randomise or mutate d.Req.Id in the DoQ (or DoH) server handler before forwarding instead of in the plain-UDP upstream exchange

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit also carries unrelated refactors inside the same diff (toolchain bump in Makefile/bamboo/docker/go.mod, build-tag cleanup in proxy/errors*.go, slices.Contains in upstream/doh.go, strings.SplitSeq in internal/cmd/proxy.go, min()/wg.Go test tidy-ups); they are not part of the protection and were not screened.
